source_text: Non est acceptio personarum apud Deum. Tribulatio et angustia in omnem animam hominis operantis malum, Iudaei primum et Graeci; gloria autem et honor et pax omni operanti bonum.
thought_title: God shows no partiality in judgment
orientation: Origen is explaining Paul's teaching that God judges everyone by their deeds, Jew first and also Greek, without favoritism.
pass_a_gloss: Not is [there] acceptance of persons with God. Tribulation and distress into every soul of man working evil, of Jew first and of Greek; glory but and honor and peace to every [one] working good.

choices.why: Literal rendering preserves the Latin idiom for partiality or favoritism, matching the source wording exactly.
Keeps the present participle's active, ongoing force and the literal sense of operor as working or doing.
Parallels the previous phrase and preserves the dative participle's sense of the one who performs good.

choices.english: of the Jew first and of the Greek
choices.why: Retains the genitive construction and the order 'Jew first' which is theologically significant in Romans.
rejected: for the Jew first and for the Greek

bible_refs.note: Tribulatio et angustia in omnem animam hominis operantis malum, Iudaei primum et Graeci; gloria autem et honor et pax omni operanti bonum

pass_b_english: There is no acceptance of persons with God. Tribulation and anguish come upon every soul of a human being working evil, of the Jew first and of the Greek; but glory and honor and peace come to everyone working good (Romans 2:9-10).
